lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Date ranges, punctuation, capitalization, and number formatting need to be standardized across entries.
Use U.S. English consistently.
items.because: The résumé mixes a U.S. context with British spellings.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are not normally needed on a U.S. résumé and can expose personal information or invite irrelevant bias.

items.says: Clarify whether the MBA is completed or expected.
items.because: The answer depends on your status.

items.says: Make the MBA date format consistent with the rest of the résumé.
Check whether the location and dates are formatted consistently with the MBA entry.
Clarify whether the 35% conversion gain is relative or a percentage-point increase.
Give the measurement period or comparison basis for the conversion gain.
Make sure the data supports attributing the gain to the new flow.
items.because: “After replacing” suggests causation.

items.says: Distinguish your contribution from the team's delivery.
Clarify what “two weeks ahead of plan” is measured against.
items.because: The reference may not be obvious to a reader.

items.says: Specify the currency of the chargeback-loss estimate.
Make clear that the loss estimate is annualized.
Avoid overstating your individual influence on the roadmap decision.
“Analysed” uses British rather than U.S. spelling.
items.because: The résumé should use U.S. English consistently.

items.says: Clarify your role in resolving the tickets.
items.because: “Closing 140 tickets” may sound like support execution rather than product work.

items.says: Explain what halving the open-ticket queue meant in practical terms.
The opt-in comparison reports a method but no result.
items.because: It does not tell the reader what the redesign achieved.

items.says: Do not present the opt-in comparison as causal without support.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who did not, creating selection bias.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period or baseline for the reduction in time to first payment.
Clarify whether the 2,300 merchants are the pilot population.
Check this result for overlap with the practicum bullet.
items.because: The practicum bullet duplicates a Harbor onboarding result.

items.says: The late-delivery bullet presents a changed calculation as a performance improvement.
items.because: Excluding weather-delayed shipments does not show that fewer shipments actually arrived late.

items.says: Give the measurement period for the reduction in pick errors.
Clarify whether 30% is a relative reduction or a percentage-point change.
“Coordinated” and “prepares” use inconsistent tenses for a past role.
Add the scope or impact of the recurring S&OP work.
items.because: The bullet describes responsibilities but not their result.

items.says: Consider spelling out “S&OP.”
items.because: Readers outside operations may not know it.

items.says: Clarify whether the 1,800 annual hours are measured or projected savings.
Explain how the driver-hours figure was calculated.
Clarify the period meant by “in its first year.”
Confirm that the 9 tonnes were actually redistributed.
items.because: The figure should not count food merely made available.

items.says: State the exact comparison period for weekly active-user growth.
Avoid implying that reminders alone caused user growth without supporting evidence.
Specify the period covered by the 95% pickup-slot fill rate.
Make clear that the reduction in staff-cover shifts is a weekly figure.
Reduce repeated “Launched” lead verbs.
items.because: The review says another bullet starts with the same verb.

items.says: Describe what you contributed or produced in the working sessions.
items.because: The bullet describes an activity, not an outcome.

items.says: Clarify the scope of the scheduling work.
Make clear whether you led the sessions.
Replace the passive construction with a clearer account of your contribution.
items.because: The passive wording obscures who did the work.

items.says: Clarify how broadly the intake changes were adopted.
items.because: “The changes were adopted” does not indicate the adoption scope.

items.says: Give a measurable result of the intake changes if one is supportable.
items.because: The bullet does not say what improved.

items.says: Delete the merchant first-payment bullet from the hospital practicum.
items.because: It is unrelated to the hospital project and duplicates a Harbor onboarding result.

items.says: The duplicated result describes the merchant population differently.
items.because: That inconsistency could undermine confidence in the résumé.

items.says: The product skills are broad; retain only ones you can discuss credibly.
Make sure your experience supports the A/B-testing claim.
items.because: The opt-in comparison is not, by itself, evidence of a controlled A/B test.
